html:
Montevideo is the capital of Uruguay, on a bay of the Río de la Plata. The Spanish governor of Buenos Aires, Bruno Mauricio de Zabala, began to fortify the site in 1724 to stop the Portuguese of Colonia from moving in.

Its fine natural harbour made it the base of the Spanish navy in the South Atlantic and a rival port to Buenos Aires. Settlers came from the Canary Islands and Buenos Aires, and enslaved Africans were landed there for the whole region. British troops held the city briefly in 1807.

It became the capital of independent Uruguay after the Cisplatine War and was besieged for nine years in the civil war of the 1840s. Immigrants from Italy and Spain made it a large modern city, home to about half the people of the country and to the candombe drummers of its old neighbourhoods.
